verification.differences: Every gearing field differs on all four bikes. primary_ratio: catalog 1.85 / 2.1 vs manual 3.273 (72/22). gear_ratios: NS200 2012-2016 is close on 3rd-6th (1.556/1.25/1.043/0.913 vs 1.556/1.238/1.045/0.917) but wrong on 1st/2nd (2.929/2.063 vs 2.833/2.067); NS200 BS6 differs in every gear; NS 200 2017-2024 and RS 200 carry a 5-speed set although Bajaj's own owner's manuals say '6 speed constant mesh'. front_sprocket: 16 (NS 200 2017-2024, RS 200) vs 14 (manual and both parts catalogues); 14 on the other two is correct. rear_sprocket: catalog 43 or 48 vs 39 (2013-2014 manual; 2012-2015 per Rolon) and 41 for the RS200. No source gives 43 or 48. chain: 520 agrees. Net effect: catalog top-gear overall ratio is 5.19 to 6.12 against the manual's 8.357.
verification.sanity: Manual ratios are internally consistent: 72/22=3.2727, 34/12=2.833, 31/15=2.067, 28/18=1.556, 26/21=1.238, 23/22=1.045, 22/24=0.917, 39/14=2.786, and 3.2727 x 0.9167 x 2.7857 = 8.357, exactly the printed overall ratio. Rear tyre 130/70-17 (manual): nominal circumference 1.928 m. Top gear with 14/39: 131.5 km/h at 9,500 rpm (the manual's power peak), 135.0 km/h at 9,750 rpm, 138.4 km/h at 10,000 rpm (the manual says the red-zone warning light blinks at 10,000 rpm or more; I found no rev-limiter figure). Published top speed 136 km/h (somosmoto.pe spec sheet for NS200 FI ABS 2017; moto-data.net gives 136 km/h for the 2012 200NS, uncited; motorradundreisen.de gives 135 km/h for 2020) = about 9,820 rpm in 6th: just past the power peak, which is what a correctly geared bike does. With a 41T rear the same speed needs about 10,330 rpm. The catalog's current gearing gives 180-212 km/h at 9,500 rpm in top gear, far above the real top speed: the catalog values are physically wrong, the manual values are plausible.
